note: Files: S3 r5/day1_hard328-01 e72c (base cue) and 86ef (RL plain) answers.jsonl, fetched to runs/theory-tests/r5/day1_hard328-01/<job>/answers.jsonl. Neither file has the field n_tok_p_lt_1e2 in any of its 328 rows (I checked field names only; the day1 jobs predate the run_cell.py change that writes it), so the script prints not_computable. The 'drop a problem if the field is missing' clause, read literally, would drop every problem and leave 0/0, which is also not computable; I did not count that as refuted. If the field were present: one row per problem_index (smallest attempt, else first in file order; neither file has an attempt field), cap_hit must be exactly False in both files, ratio of pooled rates, bootstrap over paired problems. alt_measured = ratio of the mean per-row rates.

File: e72c answers.jsonl only. Same missing field n_tok_p_lt_1e2, so the result is not_computable. If the field were present: wrong = score_v3 != 1 (null counts as wrong), quartile = floor(4r/N) over rows sorted by (n_generated, problem_index), skip a quartile with no wrong rows, no right rows or rR == 0, average ratio_q weighted by wrong count. The bootstrap resamples rows and rebuilds the quartiles each time. n = the smaller of the wrong and right groups. alt_measured = one pooled wrong/right ratio with no length matching.

Files: e72c and 86ef. Same missing field, so the result is not_computable. The field check runs before the group check, so an empty group caused only by the missing field does not count as refuted. If the field were present: base row cap_hit False and score_v3 != 1, RL row cap_hit False, d = ln((t_RL+0.5)/g_RL) - ln((t_b+0.5)/g_b), fixed = RL score_v3 == 1; refuted_without_number if a group is empty. n = the smaller of fixed and unfixed. alt_measured = difference of medians of d.
